analysis.title: US Daily: October CPI Preview
key_insights: GS expects October core CPI +0.16% m/m (consensus +0.2%) and headline CPI +0.21% (consensus +0.3%), with food +0.4% and energy +0.5% lifting headline.

Year-over-year rates are not available for most CPI indexes in the October report because October 2025 values are missing from last year's government shutdown. GS forecasts November headline CPI at 3.81% y/y (September 3.74%) and core at 2.67% (September 2.56%).
GS expects airfares unchanged m/m, based on its equity analysts' tracking of online prices. The component has risen 2.5% per month on average this year on higher oil and refined product prices.

The October report includes a semiannual update to health insurance source data. GS expects meaningfully negative readings over the next six months and assumes -2.5% for October, which pulls medical care services to -0.1% m/m. PCE uses different source data, so PCE is not expected to be affected.
GS expects autos inflation to slow: used cars -1.5% (from auction prices), new cars +0.1% (negative residual seasonality), auto insurance -0.3% (from its online dataset).

BLS's method of interpolating missing October 2025 data for the updated seasonal factors adds residual seasonality. GS estimates it boosts October seasonally adjusted core CPI by 5bp, mostly in public transportation, apparel and hotels (lodging).

GS forecasts shelter at OER +0.26% and rent +0.23% m/m after last month's jump (September OER +0.35%, rent +0.25%). It estimates underlying trends are slightly below these paces, with residual seasonality adding slightly.

GS forecast for October core PCE is +0.23%, above its core CPI forecast. Reasons: used cars carry a lower weight in PCE, and PCE source data for airfares, auto insurance and health insurance are expected to show increases. PCE airfares lag CPI because PCE prices flights at consumption and CPI at purchase.
Beyond October, GS expects core CPI of about +0.1% m/m in November and December, on slowing shelter, shrinking tariff-related price increases and continued downward pressure from health insurance.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A print below consensus would point to slower underlying inflation. GS estimates 5bp of the figure is residual seasonality from the shutdown data gap.
Food (+0.4%) and energy (+0.5%) lift headline above core.
Larger than core CPI because of differing weights and source data for used cars, airfares, auto insurance and health insurance.
Up from 3.74% in September. First month year-over-year rates can be calculated again.
Base for the October comparison. Led by lodging (+2.0%), OER (+0.35%) and used cars (+0.7%).
Slowing shelter, fading tariff pass-through and health insurance declines hold core down.
Semiannual source data update drives the decline. GS expects negative readings for six months.

risk_factors: Residual seasonality from BLS's interpolation of missing October 2025 data could push seasonally adjusted core CPI higher than the underlying trend (GS estimates +5bp).
Missing October 2025 values mean year-over-year CPI rates are unavailable for most indexes in this report.
Health insurance source data updates make the October reading hard to forecast.
The GS core CPI forecast (+0.16%) is below consensus (+0.2%), so the report carries a risk of a hotter print than GS expects.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 plots CPI health insurance against a model of insurer profitability. GS expects the run rate of health insurance inflation to turn deeply negative after the semiannual source data update.
Exhibit 3 shows CPI car insurance against a model based on state-approved price changes, with GS forecasting a 0.3% decline in October. The BLS did not publish October and November 2025 index values.

Exhibit 4 shows the revision to seasonally adjusted m/m core CPI from this year's annual revisions, with the BLS approximating missing October 2025 data as the geometric mean of the September and November 2025 index values.
geopolitical: The report cites last year's US government shutdown, which left missing October 2025 CPI values and distorted seasonal factors.

tension_points.bull_case: GS forecasts core CPI at +0.16%, below +0.2% consensus, on health insurance (-2.5%), used cars (-1.5%) and flat airfares.
tension_points.bear_case: The 5bp of residual seasonality from the shutdown data gap could lift the seasonally adjusted print, and September's core was +0.33%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI print at or above the +0.2% consensus, which would mean the health insurance, used car and airfare declines did not come through as GS expects.

theme_stances.key_argument: Health insurance, used cars and airfares pull October core CPI to 0.16%, below consensus.
BLS's interpolation of missing data leaves residual seasonality that boosts October seasonally adjusted core CPI by 5bp.
theme_stances.evidence: unduly boost October seasonally-adjusted core CPI inflation by 5bp
